speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how many persons with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are currently waitlisted for placement with a Day Activity Centre (DAC); (b) what is the average waitlist time before an applicant with ASD is offered a place at a DAC; and (c) are there any plans to make more DAC places available for persons with ASD.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: I should declare, first of all, that I am a parent with a child with ASD, who would be classified as requiring high support needs.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: I am grateful for the data that has been supplied.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: And really, I have two main supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: The first is whether there are any concerns that what we see on the waitlist may not really be a true reflection of the actual demand and need for these services.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: And I say this for two factors: one, parents with ASD children want predictability in terms of the arrangements for their care, the environment that they are in.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: And sometimes, when they are on the waitlist for too long, they can decide to take the child off the waitlist because the child has gotten used to being kept at home, even though it is not ideal.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: The other factor is that DAC costs for ASD, in particular, are quite high.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: So, if you have a family that has a household income of $5,000, they are being asked to commit 40% of the household income to pay for DAC.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: So, there is a concern that the waitlist does not look so bad because it is not affordable.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think we most certainly look at the issue of capacity, not just in the uni-dimension of number of places alone.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We do look at the different disability types, the demand under each category, and also we take an island-wide view of where the availability of these centres are for each of these disability types.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is a more nuanced approach than my main reply would suggest.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But at the back-end with MSF and also with SG Enable, we do work very closely with our partners, with our colleagues in SG Enable as well as our social service agencies to understand, drill down to what are the real needs in terms of the heat map around the island.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, rest assured that we are doing a much more nuanced analysis than just capacity alone.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: With regard to whether we are prepared to work with private providers, the short answer is yes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are looking at options to see how we can vary the different service models that we are looking at today.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think one of the key principles that I really want to hark back to is to take a step back to see what is our end objective for persons with disabilities, persons who are living with autism.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And one of the key objectives is to make sure that they can continue to live in the community with the families for as long as possible.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is to say we want to delay institutionalisation for as long as possible.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Hence, that is why in the past few years, we have worked vigorously on various pilots.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Progressively over the next few years we will be setting up more of these ESHs to make sure that we can provide community connections through the provision of social activities, caregiver support, as well as referral services.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It sounds like there are many pilots and there indeed are.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But the end goal is this: that we want our persons with disabilities and special needs, we want them to not just make do in life, but we want them to be able to thrive and flourish.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On the related issue of affordability, rest assured that through the inter-agency task force that is currently headed up by Minister of State Goh Pei Ming, we are looking at that deeply in terms of affordability of services, not just the availability of services.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I think I want to close by making a call to our Members of this Chamber, as well as to the larger society, that our vision is for our persons with disabilities to flourish, to thrive and not just to survive in the community.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We can be closer to our vision when more in our society can embrace our fellow workers, our fellow students, fellow members of a community.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I call upon all Members of this Chamber to be part of this movement so that we can move the needle towards making Singapore a more caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: I appreciate the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's point about understanding different needs.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: But the question I raised was actually specifically for those who require high support needs.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: And although every parent wants to see their child learn to be more independent, the reality is that for those with high support needs, that is the most challenging category, they are going to need a lot more care.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: And yes, we all want to delay institutionalised care, but the earlier we are able to get them into a DAC where they are stimulated and they are exposed to activities, the better.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: So, at the end of the day it does come down to capacity and I know that we have a shortage of people willing to work in this area.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: I do hope that the Ministry will do more to provide more resources for that.
